phase: 1 - grooming and training end-to-end, driven in a real browser with demo data
title: Two Food screens answer a stale link badly; a third was flagged and is correct
why_this_was_looked_at: The screen sweep flagged /food/manage, /food/subscription-invoice and /food/subscription-payment as blank. Bare visits are NOT a user path - all three are only ever linked with a query parameter (app/food/canonical-food-page.tsx:21 and app/food/subscriptions/page.tsx:60-61; subscription-payment has no in-app link at all and is reached from a stored payment_link_path). A STALE or expired link is a real path, so that is what was driven.
measured_in_a_browser: /food/manage?orderId=PS-UAT-FOOD-DOES-NOT-EXIST renders a complete order page for an order that does not exist: 'PS-UAT-FOOD-DOES-NOT-EXIST · qty · not set · fulfilment not set / Order truth / Inventory reservation: not set · lot not picked / Dispatch not dispatched ...'
/food/subscription-payment?requestId=REQ-DOES-NOT-EXIST renders its header and 'Payment request' and nothing else - no explanation at all.

findings.what: loadCustomerFoodOrder returns [] for an unknown order, so setOrder(rows[0]||null) stores null - and the render path has no `if(!order)` branch. Every field goes through label(value)=String(value||'not set'), so ABSENT is drawn as an order whose fields merely happen to be unset. The screen cannot tell apart 'still loading', 'no such order' and 'a real order with nothing filled in'. This is the audit's recurring class - unknown or absent treated as a valid state - rendered as a whole page.
findings.severity: A customer following a stale link is shown a plausible order page for an order that is not there, with a Cancel control on it.

findings.what: An unknown request id produces a header and no message. Same class as P1-01: the customer is told nothing about why the page is empty.
findings.severity: Low, but it is the page a customer reaches from an expired payment link.

refuted: /food/subscription-invoice was flagged by the same sweep and is CORRECT: it reports 'Unable to load Food subscription' for an unknown id. /food/manage with NO orderId at all also renders a deliberate placeholder with a way back; the defect is specifically the unknown-id case.
why_not_fixed: Both are render branches of client .tsx components, and this repository has no harness that can render one: there is no jsdom or @testing-library (tests/partner-surface-contract.test.mjs:21 says so), and `node --experimental-strip-types` cannot load .tsx at all - 'Unknown file extension ".tsx"'. Fixing these without a regression test would put unpinned changes into a branch whose whole claim is that every fix is RED-first and sabotage-verified. Reported instead.
the_coverage_gap_itself: No .tsx render branch anywhere in this platform can be pinned by the current test suite. Every UI-state defect found so far - P1-01's refusal copy, P1-04's fixture pets, these two - had to be found by opening a browser. That is a standing gap in the suite, not a property of these three screens.
not_claimed: Only these Food screens were driven. Other screens' stale-link and not-found states have not been swept, though lib/resource-screen-state.ts is now there for them.
correction: My first probe used ?requestId= on /food/subscription-payment. That page reads renewalId, so what I measured was the NO-PARAMETER case, not an unknown id. Both are broken, and both are now fixed, but the original note described the wrong one.
fix: New lib/resource-screen-state.ts: one five-state decision - no-id, loading, not-found, failed, ready - for a screen that loads one record by id. `loaded` is the field that does the work: without it 'we have not asked yet' and 'we asked and there is nothing' are the same value, and no screen can tell a missing record from a pending one. An error outranks both, so a failed request is never reported to a customer as a missing record.
app/food/manage/food-customer-management.tsx and app/food/subscription-payment/page.tsx both use it, and each now says what happened instead of drawing or omitting silently.
app/food/manage/page.tsx nests the incidents section INSIDE the order screen, so an order-scoped section cannot outlive the order it belongs to.
why_it_could_be_fixed_now: P1-08 added a .tsx render harness. Before that these were unfixable with evidence, which is exactly why they were reported and left.

red_first.P1-N02: RED - loading and not-found were the same state
red_first.P1-N03: RED - the failed state did not exist
red_first.P1-N04: RED - the initial render drew Order truth, Inventory reservation, Dispatch and a cancellation control
red_first.P1-N06: RED - the renewal payment screen rendered its header and nothing else

non_vacuity_controls_green_throughout: P1-N05 - the empty-orderId screen still renders its placeholder and a way back, so 'render nothing for everything' cannot pass

sabotage.control: loading is not distinguished from not-found
an error is masked by a stale record
the payment screen stops explaining itself

verified_in_the_browser: /food/manage?orderId=<unknown> -> 'We could not find that Food order. No Food order matches ... The link may be out of date, or the order may have been placed on a different account.' and nothing else
/food/manage with no id -> the existing placeholder, unchanged
/food/subscription-payment with no id -> 'This payment link is incomplete. Please open the renewal from your Food subscriptions, or check the link you were sent.'
not_pinned_and_why: The nesting of order-scoped sections is browser-verified only. A test for it would be vacuous in this harness: the 'does not render' half passes even against a component that drops children entirely, and the 'does render' half needs the ready state, which needs effects to have run - the limit recorded in P1-08. Said plainly rather than pinned by an assertion that cannot fail.
